title-proc.eng: Framework Agreement regarding procurement of 5 (five) categories of Operational Eyewear.

description-proc.eng: Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation (DALO) wishes to enter into a Framework Agreement regarding procurement of Operational Eyewear as well as spare parts, as the Danish Defence, the Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness and the Danish Police has a need for Operational Eyewear for their personnel (collectively “The Buyer”). The Buyer shall be entitled to use the Framework Agreement for purchase of the deliverables on the terms and conditions of the Framework Agreement. The Operational Eyewear is an essential part of the personnel's equipment and personal protection equipment, and will be used across training, educational and operational tasks both nationally and internationally. The eyewear must be able to integrate with various types of equipment and be usable with different types of headwear and related gear and must equally be useable without any headwear or related gear. The Operational Eyewear is divided into 5 eyewear categories. The tenderer shall provide DALO with a Framework Agreement covering all 5 categories: 1)Ballistic Eyewear 2)Ballistic Goggle 3)Tactical Parachute Goggle 4)Arctic Goggle 5)Ballistic Eyewear with prescription correction in the protective lenses The Operational Eyewear shall protect the personnel's eyes from various threats, including fragments, dust, sun, airborne insects and similar foreign objects as well as laser light. The Operational Eyewear is intended for operational use. Therefore, the personnel must be able to carry, put on, change configuration, stow and clean the eyewear during training and combat operations. Reg. 1) The tenderer shall offer a selection of 5 different models* of Ballistic Eyewear in order to fit most possible personnel with different facial shapes without compromising safety parameters, one of the models shall be compatible with COMM templets and such model shall be offered in three different sizes (Small, Medium, Large). Each of the 5 models of Ballistic Eyewear offered shall be of a one shield type eyewear (one lens covers both eyes). *A model = a product variant that has a uniform design, function and technical specification that distinguish it from other variants. Different sizes of the same product variant shall not be considered separate models. Reg. 2) The Ballistic Goggle shall include lenses with different properties for use in different environments and conditions. The Ballistic Goggle shall be a shield type goggle (one lens covers both eyes) and must be designed for use in combination with a helmet and shall either be equipped with an elastic retention strap or be capable of being directly mounted onto the helmet. The Ballistic Goggle must provide a close and secure fit to the face to ensure optimal protection and comfort and prevent fogging. Reg. 3) The Tactical Parachute Goggle will primarily be used by personnel in special operation forces for both training and actual military operations. Danish special operation forces will use the Tactical Parachute Goggle for educational and operational tasks, both nationally and internationally. The Tactical Parachute Goggle shall be consisting of either one shield type goggle (one lens covers both eyes) or one wrap type (two lenses covering an eye each) low profile eyewear and must be designed for use in combination with a helmet and shall either be equipped with an elastic retention strap or be capable of being directly mounted onto the helmet. The Tactical Parachute Goggle must provide a close and secure fit to the face to ensure optimal protection and comfort and prevent fogging. Lenses shall be easily removed from the primary frame and replaced with another lens. Reg. 4) The Arctic Goggle shall protect the soldier’s eyes from ex. snow, frost, sun and foreign objects. The Arctic Goggle is intended for operational use therefore, the soldier needs to be able to carry, put on, change configuration, stow and clean the systems, all during training and combat operations with gloves on. The Arctic Goggle shall be a shield type goggle (one lens covers both eyes) suitable for arctic conditions, designed for use in combination with a helmet and shall either be equipped with an elastic retention strap or be capable of being directly mounted onto the helmet. The Arctic Goggle must provide a close and secure fit to the face to ensure optimal protection and comfort and prevent fogging. The Lenses in the Arctic Goggle shall be capable of being easily removed from the primary frame and replaced with another lens. Reg. 5) The Ballistic Eyewear with prescription correction in the protective lenses will be used by Personnel for both training and operational use. The Ballistic Eyewear with prescription correction in the protective lenses can be a one wrap type low profile eyewear (two lenses covering an eye each with prescription correction in the protective lenses) and should not include an RX carrier solution. ... All Categories of Operational Eyewear must comply with MIL-PRF-32432A or equivalent, covering subject areas such as Ballistic fragmentation protection, Ultraviolet absorption, Haze/resistance to scratching/abrasion, Environment, User survivability and Chemical Resistance. The eyewear must further be assessed as a High Impact Protector in compliance with ANSI/ISEA Z87.1-2010 or equivalent. Categories 1, 2, 3 and 5 must additionally include a dark lens complying with ISO 12312-1.2023 or equivalent, and Category 5 must further comply with STANAG 2029 or equivalent regarding ballistic fragmentation protection. The specific references to the standards are further described in the tender documents. Where it says “or equivalent” above (or in the tender documents), this should be understood as equivalent or indisputably better. It is always the Supplier’s responsibility to demonstrate equivalence or improvement in relation to any requirement. For further requirements regarding standards, spare parts etc., reference is made to the tender documents.

title-proc.eng: Supply of a Material Processing System including delivery, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance

description-proc.eng: Enviro Grind specialises in the reprocessing of waste residues that would otherwise be sent to landfill. With extensive experience in processing organic residues, including wood waste, gypsum waste, and organic bio-wastes such as food waste, garden and park waste, and fish waste, Enviro Grind also has significant expertise in the development of high-value, peat-free products. Enviro Grind is a member of the consortium delivering The REGENERATE Project (REcyclinG phosphatEs and NitrogEn fRom AgriculTural rEsidues). Funded under The Shared Island Bioeconomy Demonstration Initiative, REGENERATE aims to demonstrate a scalable, circular, agricultural model that optimally harnesses and separates local agricultural residues from digestate to maximize the value derived from these nutrients. Enviro Grind wishes to procure a Material Processing System (“the System”) that will deliver the required throughput, separation efficiency, and product quality outcomes specified in this project. The scope will include the design integration, supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of the System. The System will comprise an integrated arrangement of components, including a trommel, double deck screen, wind shifters, optical sorter, hoppers, and conveyor belts, together with all supporting structures, controls, and safety systems necessary to achieve full operational functionality. The objective is to deliver high-quality material recovery, with particular focus on maximising compost yield while ensuring the effective removal of plastic films and other lightweight contaminants. The process aims to produce an organic, peat-free, phosphate-rich compost suitable for horticultural growing media.

title-proc.eng: Framework agreement for Microsoft/Adobe licenses, license management and cloud services

description-proc.eng: Background The Agency for Building Quality (DiBK) shall procure a new framework agreement for the purpose of establishing a more centralised and standardised licence management, as well as strengthened compliance reporting for Microsoft and Adobe licences, including accompanying cloud services. The need is driven by the desire for better control throughout the entire licence life cycle, reduced risk of licence deviations and increased compliance with the current licence terms. Furthermore, the procurement shall contribute to a better overview of actual use, licence coverage and cost development, as well as strengthened documentation and traceability with internal and external audits. DiBK needs licence management and reporting to be based on relevant and updated source systems and that the system supports automated processes connected to onboarding and offboarding, ordering, changes and completions. This shall ensure that the basis for awarding and recalling licences is at all times as correct and updated as possible, and that deviations can be uncovered and handled in an efficient and verifiable manner. Description of the assignment The assignment is for the establishment of a framework agreement for the delivery of Microsoft and Adobe licences, accompanying cloud services, as well as an overall service for licence management and Software Asset Management (SAM). The framework agreement shall cover the administration and operative management of the licence portfolio, including orders, changes, terminations and ongoing follow-up of licence use. The contract shall also include standardised compliance reporting, consumption and costs, so that DiBK has a good decision basis to optimise the licence portfolio. The delivery shall support license management in relevant administration areas and services, including M365, Azure and Adobe Admin Console. Automated processes shall be facilitated for awarding and removing licences based on identity and life cycle data, as well as mechanisms that support control, certification and traceability when required. The service shall be able to collaborate with DiBK ́s central systems for identity, personnel and onboarding, ordering as well as configuration and device data (i.a. Entra ID, HR system, ITSM and relevant unit and fixture sources), so that the licence documentation and reporting are consistent, assembled and verifiable across sources. Tenderers can submit a solution proposal themselves and state which systems are supported. Tenderers shall have full delivery and operational responsibility in the contract period, including user support, error handling and escalation with the software suppliers as needed. The framework agreement shall also ensure security and management requirements for access management, logging and audit tracks, as well as principles for data storage and protection of information in the delivery. André Stjernen is responsible for the contract in the Directorate of Building Quality.

title-proc.eng: Climate Change Capacity Building - Scoping Study

description-proc.eng: DLDC is seeking tenders from competent consultancy providers to carry out a scoping study with key stakeholders in Co.Donegal. The study will be restricted to community organisations located in the DLDC catchment area, which excludes Inishowen, Gaeltacht and Islands. The main purpose of the study is to identify the need for capacity building in local communities in the areas of environmental sustainability, climate action and climate change mitigation and adaptation. Key deliverables will include a detailed assessment of the current training provision available to community organisations in Donegal and to identify gaps in terms of climate related training provision. The consultant will be expected to carry out a combination of secondary desk-based research as well primary research including: • Online or telephone survey of a broad representation of community organisations to establish their current training needs and areas of training and capacity building interests. • Establishment of whether this training and capacity building is available locally, where provided and by whom etc. • In-person focus groups or interviews with a sampling of community organisations to identify needs focusing on building capacity for sustainability and climate action. The sampling should consist of a minimum of 20 community groups and should include but not be limited to Tidy Towns, Angling Associations, Men’s Sheds, Community Gardens, Environmental Groups and Social Enterprises. • The in-person focus groups and interviews should facilitate detailed recommendations to DLDC on training topics / modules that will be engaging and incorporate practical elements, preferred location, preferred duration and identification of any resources required to facilitate the key stakeholders drive positive change in the areas of climate, circular economy, sustainability, social inclusion and just transition and climate action at a local level are required. • Thought as to how community groups will be able to build capacity with the wider community should also be considered. The consultant will provide a final report with findings and actionable recommendations. The consultant will also provide DLDC with summary notes from each of the focus groups or interviews. All costs associated with the above activities including venue hire, materials and travel should be considered when preparing the tender response. The indicative budget for the delivery of this contract is €15,000 including VAT.

title-proc.eng: Tender for the services of a Strategic Energy Partner for Medite Europe DAC and SmartPly Europe DAC 26

description-proc.eng: Medite SmartPly is seeking to contract the services of a Strategic Energy Partner to assist in the decarbonisation of their energy consumption through innovative energy solutions using on-site energy services. The appointed Energy Management Partner shall assist Medite Smartply in delivering a fully integrated, measurable, and auditable decarbonisation and energy management programme, fully aligned with ISO 50001, IED, SEAI, ATEX, public procurement, and best in class industry standards. The partner must possess proven expertise in high volume process industries and demonstrate the capacity to drive innovation, compliance, and operational excellence in all aspects of site energy management. The partner must resource the scope of supply with of experienced senior energy engineers and professionals. The scope includes, but is not limited to, the following requirements: 1. Energy and Carbon Reduction Projects Development an Execution: a. Support for energy opportunities identification, development and execution including providing industry and energy knowledge and expertise to identify opportunities and progress through to delivery. b. Actively manage the Energy Efficiency Obligation Scheme EEOS in Medite Smartply including analysis of eligibility, M and V plans, credit tenders and submission reports. 2. Energy Performance Monitoring, Targeting, Analysis an Reporting: a. Review, establish and develop energy metrics and targets annually in cooperation with Medite Smartply that satisfy all requirements of ISO 50001. Targets should include SEU and SKU targets with the relevant EnPI’s. b. Provide energy knowledge and expertise to support analysis and address performance deviations, non-conformances and other energy issues. 3. ISO 50001 EnMS Certification an Development Support: a. Provide support for maintaining and advancing the ISO 500001 EnMS including gap analysis and audit preparation. MEDITE operates two Medium Density Fibreboard production lines including finishing and packaging lines at its site in Clonmel with a total production capacity of well over 400,000 m3 per annum. MDF production by its nature is very energy intensive both from an electrical and thermal energy point of view with the demand mainly cantered around the physical modifications made to the wood at several points in the process. The energy demand of the process is currently met by multiple energy sources. Electricity is imported from the grid while heat is produced by two biomass plants ,Line 1 steam boilers and Line 2 Energy Centre, as well as a gas fired thermal oil boiler. MEDITE’s energy management system has been ISO 50001 accredited since 2017. SMARTPLY recently upgraded its press technology from a multi daylight press to a continuous press to increase the total production capacity of the plant to well over 300,000 m3 per annum. The energy demand of the process is currently met by an energy plant which feeds heat directly into a single drum dryer. Production is run 24 hours a day with the line only brought down for maintenance once a month. SMARTPLY’s energy management system has been ISO 50001 accredited since 2023. MEDITE SMARTPLY have a long held commitment to reducing the carbon footprint of their manufacturing processes and have achieved a significant reduction since 2010. The Energy Conservation measures carried out over this period include LED Lighting Upgrades with smart controls, fan system optimisations, compressed air system optimisations and multiple process and thermal system optimisations. Medite SmartPly’s energy programme has delivered significant energy reduction in both plants to date; this has reduced the cost of production of MDF and OSB in the plants allowing the company to be more competitive in the respective markets

title-proc.eng: Framework agreement for moving services for Harstad municipality.

description-proc.eng: Background Harstad municipality needs a framework agreement for moving services that cover continuous and varied moving needs across units. The need arises particularly with frequent moves in municipal residences, settlements and relocation under the auspices of the Unit for integration, the Unit for Life Management and Nav, as well as reorganisations with office moving. The aim is to ensure sufficient capacity and uniform execution, so that moving assignments are carried out safely and efficiently, with careful management of fixtures, equipment and any sensitive content. The framework agreement shall simplify ordering and coordination and reduce administrative load and risk. Description of the assignment The procurement is for a framework agreement for moving services to Harstad municipality. The assignments will vary in type, extent and complexity and can include municipal residences, office premises, nursing homes and other institutions, as well as schools and nurseries. The framework agreement shall cover carrying and transport and it can include packing, marking, unpacking, handling goods, disassembly and assembly. The assignment can also include clearing, including waste management and source sorting. The services shall be provided with the necessary security and gentle handling of household appliances, fixtures, ICT equipment and other content. Tenders can be submitted for (1) removal services and (2) removal services, including washing out (moving wash). 3 parallel framework agreements will be signed, provided that there are a sufficient number of suitable tenderers and tenders. The tenderers will be ranked in accordance with the outcome of the competition. Tenderers who are ranked as no. 1 shall always be contacted first. If tenderer no. 1 is not able to deliver, the tenderer ranked as no. 2 shall be contacted. If no. 2 is not able to be delivered, the tenderer ranked as no. 3 will be contacted. The contract shall cover the needs of several municipal entities. Buildings c/o the Housing Office, Unit for Integration, Unit for Life Support and Nav are expected to be among the largest users.
